Original failure reproduced on the round-12 candidate 7f09967 (repro-f229-pyc-plant.sh). I planted gitignored sourceless docs/analysis/tools/csv.pyc and __pycache__/csv.cpython-311.pyc, invisible to git status, with a payload that writes .git/hooks/post-commit and exits 42. The old prefreeze imported it: all three analysis checks FAIL with the payload's exit, and .git/hooks/post-commit was written with orchestrator rights. On the candidate 6c61f2e the same plant is inert: prefreeze prints 10/10 PASS (every candidate-executing check '(sandboxed)'), exits 0, and no hook is written. My regression QA13-S6 passes, and my round-12 QA12-P2 now passes. Mechanism: sandbox-run.sh clones the committed HEAD (ignored and untracked files absent), then runs under bwrap with a read-only root, private /tmp, no network and env -i with PYTHONSAFEPATH=1 and PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1. Only tools/gates code (relative and node: imports only) and `python3 -I -B -c` run outside, from /. New independent cases confirm it. QA13-S1: an uncommitted tracked edit never reaches the command. QA13-S2: BASH_ENV, NODE_OPTIONS, PYTHONPATH and PYTHONSTARTUP don't reach the sandboxed command; BASH_ENV runs once, for sandbox-run.sh itself, in the caller's own environment. QA13-S3: source-repository hooks don't run. QA13-S4: an unknown revision fails before the command runs. QA13-S5: the command can write neither the source .git nor HOME. QA13-S7: the final check catches uncommitted drift. The finding's expected result allowed either (a) no execution or (b) detection. The fix implements (a), so QA12-P1 (no runner trace of the plant) still fails, by design. The threat model now discloses the orchestrator constraint (D-026).
